A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CCL-LGS and contain readable main text, equations, five tables, eleven figures, and supplementary Sections A–E. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation experiments on LERF and 3D-OVS, loss ablations, and supplementary efficiency and scale-aggregation experiments in Tables 1–5.

after.justification: V2 retains these original segmentation, ablation, efficiency, and scale-aggregation results, including the supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same two-scale mask extraction, SAM2 association, CLIP features, contrastive codebook losses, and Gaussian-field training and inference. The supplementary 3D interaction procedure is also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same four LERF scenes and four quantitative 3D-OVS scenes. Qualitative Room evaluation and the supplementary language-based 3D interaction examples are retained without changes.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain Feature-3DGS, LEGaussians, LangSplat, GS-Grouping, GOI, and 3D VL-GS. Supplementary and qualitative comparator sets also remain unchanged; Table 1 merely standardizes the capitalization of 3D VL-GS.

E3.justification: The mIoU evaluation, exclusion of Room from quantitative evaluation, model configurations, and 30,000-iteration training settings are unchanged. Supplementary efficiency and scale-comparison protocols are identical.

E4.justification: The CCL feature comparisons, pull/push-loss ablations, scale-aggregation study, efficiency analysis, and supplementary case studies are retained. Rewriting the ablation discussion adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The reporting of point estimates remains unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the qualitative result panels are unchanged. CCL-LGS retains average mIoU values of 65.6 on LERF and 95.2 on 3D-OVS, with the same rankings and supplementary findings.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(10), including rendering, codebook assignment, losses, and query relevance, remain unchanged. No theoretical result or proof is added or removed.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same claims about view-consistent supervision, contrastive codebook learning, and state-of-the-art segmentation performance. The shortened conclusion preserves these contributions.

C2.justification: The conclusion changes the named limiting components from SAM and CLIP in v1 to SAM and SAM2 in v2, explicitly including the tracker instead of CLIP. The imperfect-mask caveat and future mask-refinement direction remain, as do the other interpretations and supplementary limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation settings, model identifiers, optimizer and loss hyperparameters, supplementary hardware and timing information, and the project-page link are unchanged. No reproducibility information is added or removed.

R1.justification: Both versions retain the same 35 references and the same related-work discussion and novelty positioning. Reference reflow and comparator-name capitalization introduce no new cited work.

P1.justification: V2 shortens the ablation discussion and conclusion, makes small grammatical and terminology corrections, changes author order, and expands the affiliation to ZMO AI Inc. The section organization and supplementary prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, captions, and table structures are retained, but spacing and page flow change. Section 4.2 begins on page 7 instead of page 8, and the conclusion fits entirely on page 8 instead of continuing onto page 9. Both supplementary pages are visually identical.

improvement.justification: The shorter prose and consolidated conclusion provide light editorial polish. The limitation edit changes the named dependency while retaining the same imperfect-mask caveat. These limited revisions leave the scientific argument, supporting evidence, reproducibility information, and complete supplement essentially unchanged, without a meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
